claims.text: The catalyst initially has a predominantly metallic platinum surface.
Transient formation of surface platinum oxides governs the catalyst's enhanced ethanol-oxidation activity.
Transient formation of surface platinum oxides governs the catalyst's enhanced selectivity.
Transient formation of surface platinum oxides governs the catalyst's enhanced durability.
Surface platinum oxides create active sites that facilitate ethanol adsorption and activation.
Surface platinum oxides facilitate activation of ethanol-derived intermediates.
A mild oxidative pre-treatment will partially oxidize the platinum surface relative to a reductively pre-treated baseline.
Surface platinum oxide species, and possibly adjacent oxygen vacancies, act as catalytic active sites.
Induced surface oxides enhance binding and activation of ethanol and its intermediates.
Induced surface oxides reduce poisoning of the catalyst surface.
Induced surface oxides promote complete 12-electron oxidation of ethanol.
A purely metallic platinum surface preferentially accumulates poisoning intermediates that deactivate the catalyst over time.
Oxidatively pre-treated catalysts will have higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the metallic-state baseline.
Oxidatively pre-treated catalysts will show greater selectivity toward complete oxidation products such as carbon dioxide.
Oxidatively pre-treated catalysts will show improved durability over oxidative cycles.
The proposed effect should dominate when oxygen partial pressure and temperature sustain a stable but dynamic equilibrium between metallic and oxidized platinum states.
The proposed performance improvement should diminish or vanish under strongly reducing conditions.
The proposed performance improvement should diminish or vanish at temperatures that compromise platinum-oxide stability.
